comment: Which boss icon belongs to a boss arena, for the arenas whose NAMES do not already say it.
WHAT THIS IS FOR. A boss arena is found in the shape of the ground long before anything is
standing in it (TerrainLandmarks), and the icon sheet carries the game's own art for about
thirty of them - IgnagdukBossActive, IsleOfKinBossActive, G4_3_1_BossActive. Putting the two
together means the marker is the boss's own picture from the moment the area loads, which is
the whole point: by the time the monster exists, the walk there has already been decided.
MOST OF IT NEEDS NO ENTRY HERE. BossIcons derives candidate names from the area id and the
tile path and takes whichever the sheet actually carries, so the eight G4_* areas and every
arena under a folder named for its boss resolve with nothing written down. This file is for
the rest: the arena whose tile and area are named one thing and whose icon is named another.
IT SHIPS EMPTY ON PURPOSE. Every pair in here is a claim about which boss lives in which
area, and a wrong one draws the wrong boss - which looks deliberate and is invisible to
whoever wrote it. Nothing is guessed from a name that merely reads plausibly; an arena that
resolves to nothing keeps the ordinary marker, and is written to logs/boss-arenas.tsv with
its area id and tile path so the missing pair can be added after somebody has SEEN which
boss stood there.
THE VALUE IS THE ICON FAMILY, not the finished cell name: 'IsleOfKinBoss' rather than
'IsleOfKinBossActive'. Active and Inactive are chosen at draw time - the arena flips to the
Inactive art once its boss has been put down - and a family with only one picture in the
sheet is used for both. Cell NUMBERS deliberately do not appear: the sheet grows when new
art is added and every number after the insertion point would move, while a name stays a
name (see IconNames, which reads assets/icon-names.tsv).
A PICTURE THE GAME DOES NOT DRAW ON ITS MAP still works here, which is what this file is
most useful for. Not every boss has a minimap icon, but every boss has a MODEL - see
MonsterModel and MonsterPortrait, which walk the mesh, skin and rig out of the game's own
bundles - so a portrait rendered from it and laid into a cell of the sheet is a picture
like any other by the time it gets here. Name that cell '<Something>BossActive' and it
resolves with no entry at all; name it anything else and one line here binds it, because a
value is tried as a family first and then as a cell name exactly as written.
KEYS. 'tiles' is keyed by the arena tile's own path, with or without the .tdt on the end,
and is the more precise of the two - it names THIS arena rather than everything in the area.
'areas' is keyed by the area's id the way the game gives it, 'G4_3_1' or 'MapBluff', and
covers an area whose arena tile is named nothing in particular. Both are matched without
regard to case, because one side comes out of memory and the other was typed by hand.
'names' is keyed by the icon FAMILY and holds what the game calls that boss - 'SaphiraBoss'
to 'Saphira, The Dread Consort'. It becomes the arena marker's label, in place of the name
derived from the tile file ('Plantaton Boss'), and it is keyed by the family rather than by
the area because one boss is often the boss of several maps: Saphira stands in Grimhaven and
in Epitaph, and the name should not be written down twice with two chances of disagreeing.
A name works on its own - the label changes as soon as it is written, whether or not the
picture it points at has been laid into assets/icons.png yet.
'skip' lists areas somebody has looked at and found no boss picture to make: hideouts, the
Precursor towers, the hubs. It exists because the tool now lists the endgame maps that still
need one (Markers -> Map & Places), and that list is worked off the game's own 173 maps -
so the rows that will never have a boss have to be tickable off by hand. A rule that hid
them by their tags would hide exactly the maps a new league adds.
THE TOOL WRITES THIS FILE, which is what the entries above are for. Pose a boss in the
Monster Book's model pane, press PNG, fill in the area, tile and name in the window that
opens with the pictures, and press write: the four PNGs go to exports/ and the entry comes
here. This comment block is read and written back, so it survives that - do not remove it
thinking it is decoration.
